chapter: Building the band, Ivie Anderson and touring
title: Early recordings and recording under different names
summary: Greer discusses early records including 'Creole Love Call' with Adelaide Hall.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You all were starting to make some records during this time, weren't you?
I think you recorded -- let's see,
you recorded 'East St. Louis Toodle-Oo', 'Birmingham Breakdown,' I think you played --
: Didn't you all record -- you all recorded under a lot of different names, though, didn't you.

Oh, yeah, we recorded -- we recorded, not just under Duke's name. We would cut the band up and record with different people. But I -- and we made so many records, it's hard to recollect now. It's impossible.
I know one of the first records we made, Adelaide Hall sang, a long time ago.
Yeah, Adelaide, she lives in London now. She recorded, that was --
: Was she working with the band at that time or did you just bring her on.
We didn't have no soloist no. We just got an extra to record with the band. We never had no woman/vocalist.
: Until you got -- until Ivie Anderson came with the band.
